title: Run-ledger MAX_AGE reaps a live bench entry past 60 min
body:
## Summary
activeRuns() reaps any entry older than MAX_AGE_MS (60 min) even when its pid is alive, so a long bench stops counting as contention while it is still running.

## Description
tools/lib/run_ledger.mjs:95 reaps on `now - start > MAX_AGE_MS`; the `bench` entry from tools/bench/run.mjs:127 spans the whole bench. At --secs=300 that is 3 runs x 4 scenarios x ~320 s, about 64 min, so the entry is deleted mid-bench and other lanes read the machine as quiet. The fix is a heartbeat: refresh the entry periodically and age it by mtime.

## Flow
- bench --secs=300 runs past 60 min
- another lane calls contention(): the entry is reaped
- its scenario budgets get judged on a busy machine

## Expected impact
Lanes running long benches stop being invisible after 60 min. Risk: a heartbeat timer that outlives its run.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - contention stays accurate for runs over 60 min
Before: an entry with start 61 min ago and a live pid is reaped (existing test pins this)
After: predicted kept while the heartbeat is fresh
Method: simulation - defaults (~20 min) never hit it; lanes use --secs<=60 per docs/
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: run_ledger.test: an alive entry with start > MAX_AGE but a fresh heartbeat mtime must survive activeRuns

title: run_parity crashes with a stack trace on a truncated result file
body:
## Summary
runParity() calls JSON.parse on parity-result.json with no guard, so a partial write becomes an uncaught exception and the evidence run dies.

## Description
tools/tests/run_parity.mjs:25 `JSON.parse(readFileSync(out))`. A Godot killed while writing, or a full disk, leaves a partial file. The evidence run then aborts instead of writing a `parity: unreadable result` envelope.

## Flow
- parity Godot is killed mid-write
- JSON.parse throws
- tools/evidence/run.mjs aborts and later kinds are never written

## Expected impact
Evidence keeps going with a failing parity row instead of no rows. Risk: none.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a broken result fails the kind, not the whole run
Before: an uncaught SyntaxError (by reading the code)
After: {ok:false, summary:"parity: unreadable result"}
Method: simulation - runParity has no seam to inject a Godot result; that seam is the instrument
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: split a pure judgeParity(res, text) and unit-test it with a truncated text

title: class_cache.isStale throws if a .gd file vanishes mid-scan
body:
## Summary
isStale() lists files, then statSync/readFileSync each one; a file deleted in between throws ENOENT, which rejects ensureImport, and runGodot then crashes the runner.

## Description
tools/lib/class_cache.mjs:71-72 and tools/lib/godot.mjs:155. A lane editing its worktree while a runner starts (a rename or a git checkout) can hit this. The fix: treat any fs error during the scan as stale, with the reason named.

## Flow
- scanGd lists a.gd
- a.gd is renamed before the statSync
- ENOENT propagates out of runGodot

## Expected impact
Runners degrade to an import instead of crashing. Risk: a slightly more eager import.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience
Before: an ENOENT throw (by reading the code)
After: {stale:true, reason:"... changed during the scan"}
Method: simulation - the race is not deterministic; an injectable fs is the instrument
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: isStale(projectDir, fs) with a fake fs whose stat throws ENOENT for one listed file

title: Five runner CLIs each hand-roll argument parsing
body:
## Summary
run_unit, run_scenarios, bench, run_parity and release_compile each carry their own parseArgs and UsageError class; a shared tools/lib/cli.mjs would make the next runner strict by default.

## Description
Count: 5 UsageError classes and 5 parsers (tools/tests/run_unit.mjs:30, tools/tests/run_scenarios.mjs, tools/bench/run.mjs, tools/tests/run_parity.mjs, tools/tests/release_compile.mjs), after this round made all five strict. A spec-driven parser (flag -> {key, validate}) removes about 60 lines.

## Flow
- add tools/lib/cli.mjs parse(argv, spec)
- migrate the five runners
- runner_args.test.mjs stays the gate

## Expected impact
Shrinks duplicated code and makes the next tool strict by default. Risk: a behaviour drift in one runner, caught by the existing tests.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - 5 parsers -> 1
Before: 5 parsers / 5 UsageError classes
After: 1 parser + 5 specs (predicted)
Method: simulation - an M cross-file move into tools/lib (context tool-selftests)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: tools/tests/runner_args.test.mjs (already 5/5) run unchanged against the migrated runners

title: run_scenarios failure summary is missing a space after the exit text
body:
## Summary
The failing summary renders as "exit 1, 12.3 s,2 of 40 failed".

## Description
tools/tests/run_scenarios.mjs:107 template `${describe(res)},${failed}`. This summary goes into the evidence envelope that PoF and the lanes read.

## Flow
- a scenario fails
- summary: "exit 1, 480.2 s,1 of 40 failed (x)"

## Expected impact
Cosmetic. Risk: none.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - readable summary
Before: "s,1 of"
After: "s, 1 of"
Method: simulation - the summary is not a pure function yet; extracting it is the instrument
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: export a pure summarize(first, settled, res) and unit-test it
